subtopics.title: Constitutional Status and Powers of the ECI
subtopics.summary: The Election Commission of India is a permanent, independent constitutional body under Articles 324 to 329 (Part XV), established in 1950. It administers elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, the President and the Vice President, and has been a three-member body since 1993. Its powers are administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial, and the Supreme Court in Mohinder Singh Gill (1977) treated the case as a cornerstone for its plenary powers.
facts: Permanent, all-India, quasi-judicial and independent constitutional body
Constitutional basis: Articles 324-329 (Part XV)
Ensures free and fair elections for Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice President
Three members since 1993: one CEC and two ECs
Administrative power: defining constituencies, preparing voter lists, scheduling elections
Advisory power: advises the President and Governors, guides during emergencies
Quasi-judicial power: resolves disputes over party recognition, allocates election symbols
Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1977): cornerstone case on ECI's plenary powers under Article 324
Where laws are silent (Articles 327 and 328), ECI can act independently to safeguard free and fair elections
ECI can order a re-poll if the purity of the electoral process is compromised; judicial review usually comes after the election

subtopics.title: Appointment, Tenure and Removal of CEC and ECs
subtopics.summary: The CEC and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 replaced the 1991 Act and provides for appointment by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee, following the Supreme Court's directive in Anoop Baranwal vs Union of India (2023). The CEC and ECs enjoy Supreme Court Judge-level salary and benefits. The CEC serves for six years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and is removed through the same process as a Supreme Court Judge.
facts: Anoop Baranwal vs Union of India (2023): five-judge bench directed appointment on the advice of a Selection Committee
Earlier, the President made appointments on the advice of the Prime Minister
The 2023 Act replaced the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991 on conditions of service and transaction of business
Selection Committee: Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
Search Committee, headed by the Minister of Law and Justice, proposes a panel of five names
Selection Committee can consider names beyond the shortlist and can function despite vacancies
Tenure: six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier; not eligible for re-appointment
An EC appointed as CEC: combined term as EC and CEC must not exceed six years
CEC and ECs enjoy Supreme Court Judge-level salary and benefits
CEC is removed by the same process as a Supreme Court Judge

subtopics.title: Electoral Rolls, SIR and the Right to Vote
subtopics.summary: An electoral roll is the official list of persons eligible to vote in a jurisdiction, and being listed on it is a legal prerequisite for casting a vote. Rolls can be revised intensively, summarily or in special cases. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a focused, time-bound house-to-house verification by Booth Level Officers, and courts have held that deletion from rolls cannot rest on mere suspicion.
facts: Electoral roll: official list of individuals eligible to vote in a given election within a jurisdiction
Being on the electoral roll is a legal prerequisite for casting a vote in India
Publishing and updating rolls: ECI, state's Chief Electoral Officer, and state election commission
Article 325: no individual excluded from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
Intensive revision: complete fresh preparation of rolls through house-to-house enumeration
Summary revision: routine annual updating of existing rolls
SIR: house-to-house verification by BLOs to add missing voters, remove ineligible ones and correct entries
Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995): guidelines allowing deletion on mere suspicion struck down
Kuldip Nayar vs Union of India (2006): right to vote is statutory, not fundamental
Bihar SIR: those not in the 2003 rolls had to submit any of 11 listed documents to prove birth date or place

subtopics.title: EVM and VVPAT
subtopics.summary: The Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) records votes in place of ballot papers and boxes, and was first used in Paravur, Kerala, in 1982. The VVPAT prints a slip that lets voters verify their vote; the slip stays visible for seven seconds before dropping into a sealed box. In 2019 the Supreme Court ruled that VVPAT slips of five EVMs in every constituency should be counted instead of just one.
facts: EVM: electronic device used to record votes in place of ballot papers and boxes
First used in Paravur Assembly Constituency, Kerala, in 1982
Developed by Bharat Electronics Ltd (Bangalore) and Electronic Corporation of India Ltd (Hyderabad)
Two parts: Control Unit (with Polling Officer) and Balloting Unit (in voting booth)
VVPAT slip shows the serial number, candidate name and symbol
Slip is visible through a transparent window for 7 seconds, then is cut and falls into a sealed drop box
VVPAT machines can be accessed by Polling Officers only
VVPAT first introduced in the Noksen Assembly bye-election, Nagaland, in 2013
VVPAT used in all constituencies in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections
2019 Supreme Court ruling: VVPAT slips of 5 EVMs per constituency to be counted instead of 1

quizzes.passage: The Election Commission of India is a permanent, all-India and independent body that conducts elections across the country. Its basic task is to ensure that elections to the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies are free and fair, and it also oversees the elections of the President and the Vice President. Since 1993, the Commission has been a three-member body. It consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, who together carry out its work. The Commission shares responsibility for electoral rolls with the state chief electoral officers and state election commissions. An electoral roll is the official list of people eligible to vote in a given election within a specific area, and being on that list is a legal requirement for casting a vote. Its work involves preparing voter lists and managing polls, and it also has functions that the Constitution and the courts have helped to define. Because its powers are rooted in the Constitution, the Commission is described as a constitutional body. Its members also enjoy fixed service conditions that cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment. The Commission's responsibilities cover the whole country, including every state and union territory.

quizzes.passage: The Electronic Voting Machine, known as the EVM, is an electronic device that records votes in place of the traditional ballot papers and ballot boxes. The machine has been used in elections to the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and by-elections, and it has been in use across different parts of the country for several decades. Since it is electronic, votes are stored in the machine rather than being collected and counted manually from paper. A companion system, the Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, is attached to the EVM and is meant to give voters a way to check their choice. When a vote is cast, a paper slip is generated, and the slip lets the voter see the choice made before it is stored. The system is described as an independent unit that works alongside the EVM. The purpose of this arrangement is to increase confidence in the voting process among voters and political parties alike. Courts have also commented on the role of such systems in elections, and several judgments have discussed them. The overall aim is to make the physical record of each vote available for verification. Its use expanded gradually over the following years, and it was extended to elections across the country.
